limitations: No cyclone tracks exist for these PlaSim simulations, so the sea-level-pressure panel shows no tracks.
Sea-level pressure is the postprocessor's reduction of PlaSim surface pressure to sea level; over high ground it is an extrapolation.
Z500 anomalies are relative to a daily day-of-year climatology of a separate 110-year PlaSim control run, applied unchanged to each 6-hourly snapshot. Winds and sea-level pressure are full fields.
Frames are instantaneous 6-hourly model states; the event definition (D, s*, the peak patch, the centre and its region) uses daily means.
Fields are on the model's T42 grid (2.8 deg), bilinearly interpolated for display; north of 87.9 N and south of 20.9 N the nearest row is repeated.
Coastlines are Natural Earth 1:110m, for orientation only; the model's own T42 land-sea mask is coarser and is not drawn.
